lens: digital dawah / Muslim youth — 90-second test, shareable unit, persona pull, overlap ledger

critiques.notes: Bro, this is the one — 'when life got easy you became they; in the storm you finally said You' is a screenshot waiting to happen, and the classical warrant (Jalalayn verbatim) is airtight. Only problem: it's the SAME article as HASAN-3, so the orchestrator picks one and merges the best framing. The cross-passage map is honestly flagged modern — keep that discipline.

The ring is real and textually explicit — Yusuf literally says 'this is my dream from before,' which teaches readers what a ring IS. But this is one of THREE copies of the same piece (HASAN-5, YASMIN-5), and we just shipped a Yusuf article this week — the surah is getting crowded. The agreement-grammar half needs careful setup or Sara taps away at paragraph two.

'One grammatical move, two destinations' is genuinely sayable, and pairing 89:27-30 with 32:14 keeps it from reading fear-only. But the al-Fajr tadabbur already owns half of it, and the hellfire second-person address is a heavy landing for the 11pm scroller who arrived raw — the house tone has to carry this or it reads like a khutbah threat. Ships only if the cross-surah pairing stays the spine.

'They said one hand; He answered with two' travels — that's a real shareable unit serving the contested-verse funnel, and it opens al-Ma'idah. But two grammar cases in one piece fails my 90-second test; the Ya-Sin half dilutes the punch when 5:64 alone carries an article. Divine-attributes territory means one loose sentence gets quote-farmed — the bila-kayf boundary has to be paragraph two, not a footnote.

The idha-vs-in point is real nahw and 'the Quran calls prayer a when, not an if' is a decent line — but let's be honest about who clicks a wudu-particle article: Khalil and Yusuf, nobody else. No search intent, no contested pull, no story, no screenshot. Clean newsletter material, weak standalone acquisition piece; ship mid-priority.

Maximum reach — everyone recites this 17 times a day, and the answered-du'a seam is the most shareable reveal in the pool. But this version carries the most freight of the THREE Fatiha copies: the 1:4-arithmetic-middle ring is count-dependent, and the honest Hafs disclaimer, while right, hands an adversarial reader a thread to pull. YASMIN-6's leaner cut of the same piece is the safer ship.

'God dropped the messenger relay and answered you Himself' — that's an Amina headline and a Ramadan evergreen that gets re-shared every Sha'ban. The 79:42 exception handling is exactly the rigor that keeps Khalil's trust. Watch the 23:108 half though: 'The Door That Closes' already lives in that room, so lean hard on 2:186 and demote the second pole to a coda.

The ma/man essence-vs-attributes point is real and citable, but the risks list missed the biggest landmine: /posts/musa-firaun-dialogue-gaslighting-quran already walks this exact throne-room exchange word by word — on top of Grammar of Tyranny and the Mirror piece. That's a crowded corner of the site. Seminar-Yusuf loves it, nobody screenshots it; if it ships at all it survives only on the Jalalayn 'mismatched jawab' line the existing articles don't name.

Same article as ZAYNAB-1 and this is the slightly better spec — verbatim Jalalayn plus Kashshaf-as-paradigm stated with citation discipline, and Sara's sayable line is already written. Inaugurating iltifat as a named site category is franchise thinking, not one-off thinking. Pick this version, fold in Zaynab's four-passage map as the flagged-modern coda.

THE contested-search acquisition piece in the pool — 'does Islam blame Eve' is a perennial query with real volume and no rigorous English answer. Hasan's version wins over YASMIN-1 because the 20:122 election-and-tawbah counterweight is built in, so it can't be flipped into 'the Quran blames Adam instead' by a bad-faith screenshot. Sara reads it with her 14-year-old — that's the WhatsApp forward.

Best-written of the three Yusuf dream-ring copies — the two-tier labeling is explicit and Sara's WhatsApp line ('the grammar already told you the stars were people') is pre-baked. Docked on freshness only because a Yusuf piece shipped this week and this pitch exists in triplicate in the pool. If the trio collapses to one, collapse it to this.

The right instinct — lead with the attested munasaba (al-Razi, Ibn al-Qayyim) and demote the count-dependent ring to a flagged aside. 'You ask to be guided; the next sentence is the guidance' is Sunday-school-usable, zero Arabic prerequisite, zero contested territory. Of the three Fatiha copies, this and YASMIN-6 are near-tied; YASMIN-6 is marginally cleaner by cutting the ring entirely.

Same target as HASAN-4 with identical audience pull — but the framing runs hotter: 'if the disobedience-verb lands anywhere, it lands on the man' is exactly the transferred-blame overreach Hasan's version fences off, and 20:122's immediate election of Adam goes unmentioned. That's the sentence that gets screenshotted against us. Merge into HASAN-4's more careful chassis, keep Yasmin's comparative-dignity guardrails.

Bro, the overlap correction caught the wrong article. The real killer is /posts/the-son-who-said-do-what-you-are-commanded — the published piece's TITLE is this proposal's core reveal, and the-patience-of-ismail covers the scene a second time. Per the ledger's own rule that's dead on arrival as-is. The interrogative-unzur + dual-aslamaa grammar is genuinely uncovered, but this must be rebuilt as a narrow structural addendum citing both existing pieces, not shipped as proposed.

Three published articles already own this exact beat: 'The Father Who Waited' (grief-to-blindness), 'Ya'qub's Intuition: The Father Who Knew What He Could Not Prove' (disbelieving the wolf story — literally this thesis), and 'Sabr Jamil.' The only new molecule is the Genesis comparison, and a Genesis coat on a thrice-told story is not an article. Kill it, or fold one comparative paragraph into a future intertextual roundup.

5:32 misquote traffic is real, perennial, and exactly our proven acquisition channel — and quoting the verse IN FULL with its addressee named is the credibility move that separates us from sermon posters. One flag the proposal missed: the site's 5:32 tadabbur is arguably our best-known page (I sent it to my own students), so this article must cite and differentiate from it explicitly or it reads like self-plagiarism. The Mishnah Sanhedrin parallel included openly, not hidden, is what makes Yusuf cite it on a panel.

Third copy of the Yusuf dream-ring and the most academic cut of the trio — Yasmin's own persona table admits Amina and Sara sit at 3. Citation-dense is great for Khalil, but citation-dense is not a landing pattern for the 16-year-old. Accurate and shippable; if only one ring piece survives, HASAN-5's framing beats this on shareability.

My pick of the whole batch. Cleanest of the three Fatiha copies: single exhibit, sidesteps the verse-count arithmetic entirely, attributed classical sources, and the most sayable line in the pool — 'you ask to be guided; the next thing God says is: here is the guidance.' This is the first article a brand-new reader should ever meet, and the one where every persona scores 4+. Ship it first and build the quote card the same day.
